- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong bearish momentum, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply lagged mean reversion to recent low.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending downward; increase forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values if sentiment is volatile.
- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and price is trending upward, model may overfit recent highs; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
